title: Ocarina
summary: The ocarina is a vessel-shaped flute with finger holes, made from clay, found in the Americas, China and Europe. Instead of a long tube it has a rounded body: the player blows across the edge of a small window and covers holes to change the pitch, and the whole vessel rings with a soft, pure tone.
howToPlay: A covered hole glows; an open hole shows its dark bore. Eight notes of the scale are lit across the body of the clay vessel.
Each strike shows the fingering of that note and a band of breath runs from the mouthpiece to it.
Strike close to the beat; a long note swells slowly.
rules: A phrase is a line of notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: Clay vessel flutes have been made for thousands of years, from small bird-shaped whistles to the sweet-potato ocarinas of today.
